description: Build a daemon that keeps /home/workspace/shared/sft/runpod_session.json fresh and emits mesh_events when the active RunPod SFT pod becomes unreachable. Single credential: env var `zocomputerRPMay` (exact case; this is the SSH private key contents OR a path to the key file — daemon should accept either by checking if the value starts with '-----BEGIN' for inline key, else treat as filesystem path). The runpod_session.json is authored manually by Robin (or a future tower task) with shape: {pod_id, pod_name, public_ip, ssh_port, gpu_type, started_at}. Daemon DOES NOT discover pods on its own (no RunPod API token available). Every 5 minutes: (1) read runpod_session.json; if missing, log INFO once and sleep — do not crash. (2) if present, attempt an SSH liveness probe using `zocomputerRPMay` against ssh -i KEY -p PORT -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no root@PUBLIC_IP 'echo OK' — capture stdout/stderr/exit_code. (3) write probe result (ssh_reachable bool, latency_ms int, last_verified_at ISO-8601, last_error str|null) back to runpod_session.json atomically (temp+rename). (4) heartbeat to service_health every 60s on a daemon thread. (5) On state transition reachable→unreachable, ws_write a mesh_event severity='error' event_type='runpod_pod_unreachable' with the pod_name and last_error. On unreachable→reachable, severity='info' event_type='runpod_pod_recovered'. Constraints: FileHandler ONLY (no StreamHandler), ws_write only for DB writes (never direct duckdb.connect), ISO-8601 string timestamps, idempotent. Closes the gap that one-shot SCP-back scripts can't recover from a dead pod silently. Reference one credential name `zocomputerRPMay` consistently in all log lines and error messages — never invent alternate names like RUNPOD_API_TOKEN.
